clauses.text:
Sec. 2. In addition to the plans re­
quired by section 1  hereof, each Federal

=== PDF page 6 of 48 ===
3478 THE PRESIDENT
department and agency shall prepare 
plans for maintaining the continuity of 
its essential functions at the seat of 
Government and elsewhere during the 
existence of a civil-defense emergency. 
The personnel, materials, and facilities 
required for this purpose shall be exclu­
sive of the personnel, materials, and 
facilities required for the execution of 
the plans prepared pursuant to section 1  
of this order. In the preparation of the 
continuity plans required by this section, 
each department and agency shall con­
sult with the Federal Civil Defense Ad­
ministration with respect to the civil- 
defense aspects of its functions. In order
to achieve uniformity of planning for 
the continuity of essential functions, the 
National Security Resources Board shall 
establish such standards and policies as 
it may from time to time deem desirable. 
That portion of the continuity plans of 
a department or agency which involves 
its functions at the seat of Government 
shall become effective upon approval by 
the President, and that portion, if any, 
which involves functions performed else­
where shall become effective upon ap­
proval by the head of thé department or 
agency concerned.
S ec. 3. The Federal Civil Defense Ad­
ministrator shall assist the departments
and agencies by indicating the types of 
personnel, materials, facilities, and serv­
ices considered useful for civil-defense 
purposes in time of efnergency; arrange 
for the use of such personnel, materials, 
facilities, and services as are not required 
for maintaining the continuity of the 
essential functions of the departments 
and agencies; and coordinate such ar­
rangements with national, State, and 
local civil-defense plans.
Harry S. T r xjm a n 
T he W hite H ouse, .
April 17, 1952.

circumstances, for preparation for such 
effective time; and good cause exists for 
making the provisions of this section ef­
fective as hereinafter set forth. Ship­

afforded an opportunity to submit their

this section, including its effective 
time, are identical with the aforesaid 
recommendation of the committee, and 
informatioil concerning such provisions 
and effective time has been disseminated 
among handlers of such lemons ; it is 
necessary, in order to effectuate the de­
clared policy of the act, to make this 
section effective during the period here­
inafter specified; and compliance with 
this section will not require any spe­
cial preparation on the part of persons 
subject thereto which cannot be com­
pleted by the effective time thereof.

Findings. (1) Pursuant to the market­

that the limitation of the quantity of

inafter specified; and compliance with

pleted by the effective time thereof.

versions.research_rationale: EO 10346 (signed 1952-04-17, 17 FR 3477-3478), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 civil-defense support plans under FCDA sec. 302; Sec. 2 continuity-of-functions plans, NSRB standards and approval; Sec. 3 FCD Administrator assistance and coordination. It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (4) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95). Inventory: the dossier's 8 clauses omit Sec. 1, run Sec. 2 through Sec. 3, and include seven clauses of Lemon Regulation 431 printed after the order; one override gives the 3 sections with no gap or overlap and drops the lemon regulation. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog and the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 record amendments by EO 10438 (1953), EO 10773 and EO 10782 (1958) and EO 11051 (1962), a 'See' note from EO 10529 (1954) and the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 10346 named only in EO 10438 sec. 1(c), EO 10773 sec. 4(a)(3), 4(b)(4) and its codification table, EO 11051 secs. 601(3) and 603(b), EO 10529 sec. 1 ('in consonance with the provisions of section 3 of Executive Order No. 10346', also printed in the page text of EO 10528) and its FR contents line, the contents line and heading printed with EO 10344 and 10345, and the FR page number 10346 in EO 10692 and 10693; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. The four changing orders were read and are attached as later events (EO 10438 on Sec. 2, whose penultimate sentence names the NSRB; EO 10773, 10782 and 11051 on all three sections): they move the NSRB, FCDA and ODM roles to the ODM, OCDM, OEP and Department of Defense and end nothing. EO 11051 sec. 604 revoked EO 10438, 10773 and 10782 only to the extent not already executed. EO 10529 supplements Sec. 3 and amends nothing. No order ended or suspended any clause before 1969-10-28, and no amendment of the order after EO 11051 and before 1969 exists in any held source. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions (Part 6 Post Office, Part 7 Interior, Part 8 Agriculture, Part 10 Labor, Part 11 Health, Education, and Welfare, Part 13 Transportation including civil aviation, Part 18 FCC including electromagnetic-radiation control of non-Government stations); Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 10346 in full (secs. 1-3): it required each Federal department and agency to prepare plans for providing its personnel, materials, facilities and services in a civil-defense emergency under sec. 302 of the Federal Civil Defense Act (sec. 1) and plans for the continuity of its essential functions, with standards from the NSRB (later ODM, OCDM, OEP) and approval of seat-of-Government portions by the President (sec. 2), and had the FCD Administrator assist and coordinate (sec. 3). EO 11490 sec. 102(b) re-imposes continuity planning on every department and agency under OEP guidance, and Parts 2-30 re-assign civil-defense support planning, as the consolidation sec. 101 describes; that is a new assignment, not a continuation of EO 10346. Plans prepared and approved before 1969-10-28 are completed acts of the agencies. versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10346 (17 FR 3477; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10346, Preparation by Federal Agencies of Civil Defense Emergency Plans, signed April 17, 1952, under the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950. Inventory: three sections (agency civil-defense plans; continuity-of-functions plans; assistance by the Federal Civil Defense Administrator). The dossier listed eight clauses, most of them the paragraphs and prorate schedule of a Department of Agriculture lemon regulation printed on the same page; the inventory is corrected to the three sections by absolute character spans of the held text. Ending: section 3015 of Executive Order 11490 of October 28, 1969 revokes Executive Order No. 10346 of April 17, 1952 by number (its item 4). The machine ACT record for pair 10346 and 11490 that points to section 501 is not the revoking provision; the alternative record on the American Presidency Project transcription of 11490, whose long span runs through section 3015 and contains item (4) naming 10346, is selected because the Federal Register tail text is held only as an unregistered lead and the transcription is the registered working text; its identity (heading, number and date agree), completeness (the text runs from the heading to the end of section 3015) and the page-level agreement of section 3015 item (4) with the govinfo OCR are confirmed. The U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note and the OFR catalog also report revocation by Executive Order 11490 on 1969-10-28. Amendments (later events, not ends): Executive Order 10438 (1953-03-13) transfers functions of the National Security Resources Board and its Chairman under 10346 to the Director of Defense Mobilization; Executive Order 10773 (1958-07-01) substitutes references to the Federal Civil Defense Administrator and Administration and to the Office of Defense Mobilization; Executive Order 11051 section 603(b) (1962-09-27) substitutes references to the Office of Emergency Planning or the Department of Defense. The U.S. Code note also lists Executive Order 10782 among amending orders; its held text does not cite 10346, so no event is recorded for it. Executive Order 10529 of 1954 cites section 3 of 10346 and does not amend or end it. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

(1) Executive Orders 10438, 10773 and 11051 amend references or transfer functions; amendments are later events, not ends, and none revokes or supersedes 10346. Executive Order 11051's general revocation list names 10438, 10773 and 10782, which were amending orders, not 10346 itself. (2) Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 and the abolition of the Federal Civil Defense Administration: not held as acting on this order and not naming it; under the unnamed-instruments ruling of 2026-10-21 they do not end it. (3) Executive Order 10529 of 1954 relies on section 3 of 10346 and amends nothing in it. (4) The OFR catalog and the U.S. Code note list no other revocation. EO 11490 section 3015 is the first held instrument that revokes the order. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: each of the three sections is a separate duty (plans under section 302; continuity plans; the Administrator's assistance), but none has a separate source or sunset shown in held evidence; all three are revoked together by section 3015 of Executive Order 11490.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: none after bounded search; the successor assignments in Executive Order 11490 are that order's own commands, and section 3014 does not save 10346 (it excepts section 3015).","scope_check":"Scope: section 3015 of Executive Order 11490 revokes Executive Order 10346 by number without exception; section 3014 saves other existing assignments, not 10346. It reaches all three sections. The dossier leads target provision not located: EO:10438, EO:10529, EO:10773 and EO:10782 are resolved: 10438 and 10773 are amendments recorded as later events; 10529 only recites section 3; 10782 does not cite 10346 in its held text."}

savings_residuals.reason: Section 3014 of Executive Order 11490 keeps existing assignments of functions made by statute, order or directive except as provided in section 3015, and section 3015 revokes 10346; the planning duties of 10346 were reassigned afresh by Executive Order 11490 (new sections for each department) and are not residual effects of 10346. No held source shows a continuing independent effect of the revoked order, and the agencies' completed plans carry no authority of 10346 (Executive Order 11490 section 3011 says plans confer no authority to put them into effect).

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10346 (1952-04-17; Preparation by Federal Agencies of Civil Defense Emergency Plans) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (17 FR 3477-3478), whose file also contains neighbouring orders; the order was delimited by its heading and the Harry S. Truman signature line, and the dossier's machine inventory, which spans text of other orders, was replaced with the four scopes below. Its own terms contain no end date or end condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register text of 34 FR 17567 onward. EO 10438 and EO 11051 are recorded as amendments on Section 2. EO 10773 (which restates references to the Federal Civil Defense Administrator in this and other orders) and EO 10529 (which cites Section 3 of this order) were read as leads and are not recorded as events or ends; I did not establish an effective date for the EO 10773 reference change, so it is not claimed.
